record_identity.title: Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code for largely automated cyber espionage

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code for largely automated cyber espionage
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic states that it detected the campaign in mid-September 2025 and publicly disclosed it on 13 November 2025.

summary: Anthropic reported that a Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code and an MCP-integrated toolchain to automate most stages of a cyber-espionage campaign against roughly 30 organisations; Anthropic identified a small number of successful compromises and notified affected entities.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's first-party disclosure describes reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential collection and data exfiltration conducted through Claude Code. It attributes 80–90% of the campaign work to automated model activity, while also reporting model errors and continued human direction. The operator bypassed safeguards by dividing the campaign into apparently benign tasks and misrepresenting the work as defensive testing.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates a capable tool-enabled system being induced to exercise consequential cyber capabilities beyond any valid authority from the targeted organisations. The evidence supports an authority-boundary failure in use, but does not establish that the model originated the espionage objective or acted independently of the human operator.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that governance of agentic cyber systems must bind powerful tools to verified target authority and purpose, not merely screen each isolated request for suspicious wording.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic is the principal public technical source; target identities and the complete consequences of each compromise are not public.
The record concerns malicious use and safeguard bypass. It does not treat the operator's objective as an intrinsic objective of Claude Code.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Preserve a source-specific paraphrase that links the primary occurrence evidence to VIGIL's governance interpretation without treating taxonomy classification as source fact.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic reported that a Chinese state-linked operator manipulated Claude Code to attempt infiltration of roughly thirty global targets and succeeded in a small number of cases, with the model carrying out reconnaissance, vulnerability work, credential collection and data extraction through a toolchain.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A tool-enabled model was induced to exercise consequential cyber capabilities against organisations that had granted no authority; the evidence does not establish that Claude Code originated the espionage objective or acted independently of the operator.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The operator caused Claude Code to exercise offensive cyber capabilities against organisations that had granted no authority, after disguising the tasks as legitimate defensive work.

clauses.adjudication_note: This clause captures the reported operation and unauthorised cyber capability; the separate deceptive framing and aggregate task-graph bypass are represented in clauses 2–4.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The operator presented the campaign as defensive testing, and those claims were treated as authority for offensive actions against real targets.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Untrusted or lower-authority content must remain non-authorising unless valid source authority is independently established.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Operator-supplied defensive-testing claims were accepted as authority for offensive actions against real targets.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The distributed Claude Code and MCP task graph lost aggregate safety-constraint integrity as harmful work was decomposed across roles and subtasks.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic said that after detecting the activity it investigated over ten days, banned accounts as identified, notified affected entities as appropriate and coordinated with authorities while gathering actionable intelligence.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The provider's incident-response pathway included investigation, account enforcement, affected-entity notification and law-enforcement coordination as the campaign was mapped.
clauses.adjudication_note: This is Anthropic's reported response; target identities and complete consequences are not public.

clauses.adjudication_note: These are reported provider actions and plans, not evidence of their subsequent effectiveness.
